title: One LCP routine family serves the builder, the search and the file
body:
Five pieces of code compute a longest common prefix, with three different contracts.

- `lcp::lcp` (`libsufr/src/lcp.rs:79`) takes two byte slices and an optional `LcpCache`, has an AVX2 path, and is called only by the builder. `lcp_scalar` (`:134`) is its tail.
- `SuffixArrayBuilder::find_lcp` (`sufr_builder.rs:270`) takes `len` as the maximum length and handles the seed mask and max query length.
- `SufrFile::find_lcp` (`sufr_file.rs:362`) takes `len` as the absolute end of the text. It is scalar and ignores the mask.
- `SufrSearch::compare` (`sufr_search.rs:244`) compares a query with a suffix, handles mask and max query length, and has its own scalar loop (272-276).
- `util::find_lcp_full_offset` is the seed-mask helper that the builder (713) and `compare` (321) share.

The `SuffixSortType` `match` on `Mask` versus `MaxQueryLen` appears at `sufr_builder.rs` 280, 383, 686 and 890/909, and at `sufr_file.rs` 487-510. A builder TODO at 278 notes it.

## Proposal

One LCP routine family in `lcp.rs`. It takes a mask and max query length where they apply, keeps the AVX2 path, and has one contract for what `len` means. The builder, the search and `SufrFile` call it, and the other four are deleted. The sort-type decision is made once and passed in.

Builds and searches must give identical results. The AVX2 path must not get slower, which needs a benchmark on a large input before and after.
